hook.line: I had 30,000 girls on my email waitlist before drop day, and here's how.
hook.visual: Founder in a striped robe, selfie framing in a wood-panelled room; small native title 'how to sell out your brand' above her head, tiny captions at chest level.

beats.what: Result first: 30,000 on the email waitlist before launch.
Step 1: built the product in public for almost a year.
Step 2: owned a community built for her audience.
Step 3: launched a website to capture emails first.
Why email: own the list instead of relying on the algorithm.
Only cut: pivot into the sponsor read for an email platform.
Top text 'link in my bio to try it out' appears during the sponsor features.
Sponsor tie-in to AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude to see what performs.

why_it_works: Specific result in the first sentence (30,000 waitlist, sold out in five minutes) earns the 90 seconds that follow.
Close, steady selfie framing and a calm voice read as a friend's advice, which softens the sponsor read.
The how-to steps lead naturally into the product (email list -> email platform), so the ad feels like step 4 rather than an interruption.
weaknesses: Almost no visual change: one cut in 92 s and no events, all retention rests on the voice.
Captions are tiny (median 0.038 of frame height) and hard to read on a phone.
Steps are not numbered on screen, so the structure is easy to lose.
Second half is a sponsor read; viewers who came for the tips may drop.
for_robert: Open with the concrete result number before any explanation; avoid long static stretches with tiny captions - Fred popping in to mark each step would add the visual change this video lacks.
